newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields closed lower on Monday, pushed by stronger foreign markets, a firmer crown and expectations of a Riksbank repo rate cut at its regular tender.
Six-month T-bill rates dropped seven basis points to 4.94 percent while nine-year bond yields fell three basis points to 8.10 percent.
Fourteen out of 18 economists polled by Reuters forecast a 15 basis point repo cut on Tuesday to 5.10 percent. The reamining four forecast a cut of 10 basis points.
If there was no 15-point cut, there would probably be some selling, dealers said.
The spread between Swedish and German longer yields decreased by two basis points to 176 and the crown firmed to 4.4570 against the mark compared to 4.4680 on Friday.
Handelsbanken economic forecasts released on Monday had no impact on the market, dealers said.
The bank revised upward its GDP growth estimate to 1.7 percent from 1.3 percent for 1996. For 1997 and 1998, the bank estimated growth of 2.2 percent.
